title: `BlobVec` does not respect alignment for zero-sized types

labels.name: P-Unsound
labels.description: A bug that results in undefined compiler behavior

body:
## Bevy version

e48c05c73474a5f6a212257cecda7ceaf2465cf3

## Problem

Like `Vec`, `BlobVec` uses a dangling pointer as the backing storage for zero-sized types. However, `BlobVec` does not respect alignment, which results in instant UB when using a ZST with alignment other than 1.

```rust
#[test]
fn aligned_zst() {
    #[derive(Component)]
    #[repr(align(32))]
    struct Zst;

    let mut world = World::default();
    world.spawn(Zst);
    world.spawn(Zst);
    world.spawn(Zst);

    let mut q = world.query::<&Zst>();
    for &Zst in q.iter(&world) {}
}
```

[The offending line](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/e48c05c73474a5f6a212257cecda7ceaf2465cf3/crates/bevy_ecs/src/storage/blob_vec.rs#L55): it creates a dangling pointer which is well-aligned for `u8`, not for the type being stored.
